title: Flat localization in the second derived tensor factor
statement: Let $R\to A$ and $R\to B$ be maps of commutative rings, let $S\subset B$ be multiplicative, set $C=S^{-1}B$, and assume $B\to C$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $M$ be a cochain complex of $A$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. For every $i$, the canonical map $H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_B C\to H^i(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C)$ is an isomorphism of $A\otimes_R C$-modules, natural in $M$ and compatible with the derived-category actions of $A$ and $B$. It is also compatible with the comparison maps: the square formed by $H^i$ of the canonical comparison map $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R B)$ tensored with $C$, $H^i$ of the comparison map $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}C\to M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R C)$, the above isomorphism, and the canonical map $H^i(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R B))\otimes_B C\to H^i(M\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}(A\otimes_R C))$ commutes.

source.place: Tag 06Y6 (lemma-derived-base-change) with flat base change of cohomology; equation comparison-map

proof.text: For any R-complex K, baseChangeMap is flatHomologyMap followed by homology of extendCompIso [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology]. Flatness gives preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat; extension of scalars preserves cokernels as a left adjoint. Therefore flatHomologyMap is the inverse of ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso and is invertible. The second factor is the homology of an isomorphism and is invertible as well. Specialize K to the R-resolution of the restricted A-complex M. No localization assumption is needed for this step.

For a chain map f:K→L, ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality identifies the scalar extension of H(extend(R,B)(f)) followed by flatHomologyMap at L with flatHomologyMap at K followed by H(extend(B,C)(extend(R,B)(f))). Naturality of extendCompIso and functoriality of homology then give E(H(extend(R,B)(f))) b_L = b_K H(extend(R,C)(f)). Apply this to resolution(R).map(restrict(R,A).map(f)) for naturality in M. Apply the same equation to a times the identity of M for compatibility with the A-action. C-linearity and the restricted B-action are built into the ModuleCat C morphisms.

Let K=restrict(R,A)(resolution(A)(M)), q=resolution(R)(restrict(R,A)(augmentation(A)_M)), and p=augmentation(R)_K. Let l_B,l_C be cohomology of their scalar extensions of q, and r_B,r_C those of p. By spanLeft_isIso [def-pc-ring-tensor-cohomology], l_B and l_C are invertible. The preceding chain-map naturality gives E(l_B) b_source = b_middle l_C and E(r_B) b_target = b_middle r_C. The comparison map is l_B inverse followed by r_B. Precompose the required square with the invertible E(l_B). Its left side reduces to E(r_B) b_target; its right side reduces using the first equation and l_C l_C inverse = identity to b_middle r_C. These agree by the second equation. Cancelling E(l_B) proves the comparison square.
